summary: Admit the PEK request print form through the existing bounded label reader.

impacts.evidence: The existing tenant-scoped PEK account and permission path remains the source of the document request.
The bounded PDF is reduced to an opaque digest reference before leaving host transport.
The provider-neutral LabelRequest and LabelResult contracts are reused.
No event envelope, event type or event payload changes.
The existing logistics.label.read capability and SDK interface remain unchanged.
No database columns, mappings or durable provider payloads are added.
The cargo code, response size, base64 data and PDF signature are bounded before artifact publication.
The existing label permission and outbound policy continue to gate the read operation.
Existing logistics label lineage records the opaque artifact reference without PDF contents.
Repeated reads are deterministic for the same validated payload; ambiguous responses never fabricate a document.
The transport adds a bounded fixed-host HTTPS POST under the existing host-mediated egress boundary.
Existing logistics timeout, rate and error normalization covers the additional PEK print request.
Removing the PEK label format or support entry disables request-form reads without migration.
Deterministic tests verify type=big, cargo code, base64/PDF validation and the opaque artifact prefix.
